C004.name: MR
C004.definition: MR is another term called mixed reality.

C005.name: headset
C005.definition: It is worn on the head, blocks our vision, and transports us to a virtual world which we can experience through the headset.

C006.name: Immersive technologies
C006.definition: These are technologies where the user experiences an environment through sensory organs in a way that makes them fail to distinguish it from reality.

C007.name: Immersive
C007.definition: It describes a perceived experience through sensory organs that appears to be real, causing the user to assume the environment is real.

C008.name: reality-virtuality continuum
C008.definition: It is essentially referring to a scale that spans from the real environment to the virtual environment.

C009.name: real environment
C009.definition: This is one extreme of the scale where there is nothing virtual.

C010.name: virtual environment
C010.definition: This is the other extreme of the scale where there is nothing real.

C011.name: augmented virtuality
C011.definition: Augmented virtuality is the opposite of augmented reality, where we are augmenting the virtual world with real world content.

C012.name: Metaverse
C012.definition: It is a concept that reimagines how humans interact with the digital world, moving beyond flat screens into an all-around 3D environment where users interact naturally.

C013.name: AR VR systems
C013.definition: These are the technologies that students will learn how to develop and deploy to master the field of virtual reality and augmented reality.

C014.name: Application areas
C014.definition: Application areas are the different areas pertaining to extended reality that the course will cover.

C015.name: Categories of systems
C015.definition: Categories of systems are different types of systems viewed from the application point of view that are present in the market.

C016.name: Use forecasts
C016.definition: Use forecasts are predictions about the likely scenario down the line in terms of application of extended reality technology.

C017.name: virtual tours
C017.definition: Virtual tours are experiences that give the user the experience of visiting a place without physically going there.

C018.name: virtual tourism
C018.definition: Virtual tourism is a popular method that allows users to explore faraway places while saving money and physical effort.

C019.name: heritage tourism
C019.definition: Heritage tourism allows users to visit a heritage place virtually, enabling them to explore every part of the space without physically going there.

C020.name: Non-immersive VR system
C020.definition: A virtual experience obtained through a computer where the user can control characters or activities within the software, but the environment is not directly interacting with the user.

C021.name: Augmentation of real-world content with digital content
C021.definition: This is the focus of AR, which involves adding digital content onto real-world content.

C022.name: Immersive experience
C022.definition: This is a term emphasized when discussing VR, but it is not mandatory in the case of AR.

C023.name: Reconstruction of lost structures
C023.definition: This is an interesting application area where lost structures can be added to the screen using AR.

C024.name: Virtual tape measure
C024.definition: This is an augmented reality application that allows users to measure heights or lengths without needing a physical tape.

C025.name: Customer experience
C025.definition: This refers to providing customers with the ability to test or visualize products in their environment before making a purchase decision.

C026.name: Telemedicine
C026.definition: This is an option that enables medical professionals to interact with patients using AR.

C027.name: VR system categories
C027.definition: These three categories (non-immersive, semi-immersive, and fully immersive) are based on the importance of the psychological aspect and user experience.

C028.name: Marker-based
C028.definition: These systems are easier to make and rely on simple algorithms, but they are difficult to maintain unless the environment is highly sanitized.

C029.name: Markerless
C029.definition: These techniques are used to overcome marker maintenance issues and primarily rely on computer vision, sometimes utilizing other sensors.

C030.name: Superimposition-based
C030.definition: This is a type of computer vision-based application used in AR.

C031.name: Projection-based techniques
C031.definition: These techniques, such as holographic projection, can be utilized in AR application development.

C032.name: Virtual
C032.definition: Being in essence or effect but not in fact.

C033.name: Reality
C033.definition: The state or quality of being real, or something that exists independently of ideas concerning it.

C034.name: Artificial environment
C034.definition: A computer-generated environment that may be populated with artificial objects.

C035.name: Sensory stimuli
C035.definition: Computer-generated inputs, such as sights and sounds, that allow the user to experience the artificial environment.

C036.name: Interaction
C036.definition: The dynamic change in the virtual environment that occurs based on the user's actions or inputs.

C037.name: VR system
C037.definition: A system is classified as a VR system only if it satisfies all three characteristics: virtual environment, immersive experience, and interaction.

C038.name: Characteristics of AR system
C038.definition: The defining features of an AR system, which include combining real with virtual, being interactive in real time, being registered in 3D, and being experienced through sensory organs.

C039.name: Overlay digital information
C039.definition: The process of placing digital information onto a representation of reality or an image of reality that is being viewed through a device.

C040.name: Registered in 3D
C040.definition: The requirement that digital content appears at the appropriate place when enhancing reality, allowing for seamless mixing with real-world objects.

C041.name: Augmented reality system
C041.definition: AR systems are the ones which augment or enhance our sense of reality.

C042.name: Formative years
C042.definition: This phase is roughly associated with the years between 1950 and 1990.

C043.name: Modern phase
C043.definition: This phase is defined as the period between 1991 and 2015.

C044.name: Growth phase
C044.definition: This is the current phase, which roughly started from 2016 onwards.

C045.name: Stereoscopic device
C045.definition: A stereoscopic device is a tool that allows the brain to process two-dimensional images as three-dimensional objects.

C046.name: Immersion
C046.definition: Immersion is the state where 2D images are perceived as 3D objects or 3D space due to stereoscopic vision.

C047.name: Stereoscope
C047.definition: A stereoscope is a compact-sized device created to generate the illusion of depth when viewing images.

C048.name: Flight simulator
C048.definition: A flight simulator is a concept that uses multiple sensors to provide an immersive experience.

C049.name: HMDs or head-mounted displays
C049.definition: A new kind of computer display that people started working on in the 1950s.

C050.name: Sensorama
C050.definition: A device that tried to engage all our sensory organs, and is considered the first immersive virtual reality system.

C051.name: Haptic feedback
C051.definition: A sensation that allows the user to feel objects on the screen through touch.

C052.name: Virtual Visual Environment Display
C052.definition: The first commercially viable stereoscopic head-tracked HMD with a wide field of view.

C053.name: CAVE system
C053.definition: A system that renders images in a surrounding setting, giving an immersive experience.

C054.name: WTK package
C054.definition: A software package developed for higher level application development in VR.

C056.name: White 5
C056.definition: A 150-degree FOV field of view HMD.

C057.name: Oculus Rift
C057.definition: An inexpensive VR headset created in 2012.

C058.name: commercial VR headsets
C058.definition: These are well-known company releases starting around 2016 that made immersive experiences affordable to a large population, thereby spurring growth in the field.

C059.name: Experimental phase
C059.definition: This phase, which happened before the 1980s, was primarily related to early experimentation, defining concepts and showing different types of required technology.

C060.name: Basic research phase
C060.definition: This phase, occurring between the 1980s and mid-1990s, involved research into enabling technologies such as tracking, displays, and input devices.

C061.name: Tools or applications phase
C061.definition: During this phase, which ran from the mid-1990s to 2007, early applications and exploratory tasks related to interaction techniques and design theory were developed.

C062.name: Commercial application phase
C062.definition: This phase, starting from 2007 and continuing to date, is characterized by widespread AR availability and the emergence of newer applications in various domains.

C063.name: Tracking
C063.definition: Tracking technology is used to register content in 3D.

C064.name: Optical see-through head mounted display
C064.definition: This is a CRT-based display that allows the user to see through it while wearing it.

C065.name: Computer-generated imagery
C065.definition: This is imagery created by a computer that can be superimposed over the real world view or used as a substitute for the real world.

C066.name: Super cockpit program
C066.definition: This was a major program of the US Air Force that resulted in many relevant technologies for augmented reality.

C067.name: AR-type applications
C067.definition: These are precursors to the type of AR applications that are seen nowadays.

C068.name: Wearable computers
C068.definition: Wearable computers are setups where a headset is worn and the computer is carried in a backpack, utilizing various input devices.

C069.name: AR overlay on real-world markers
C069.definition: This involves using computer vision techniques to place augmented reality content onto real-world markers.

C070.name: Viewpoint tracking
C070.definition: Viewpoint tracking is the activity addressing the challenge of accurately tracking how the user's viewpoint is registered in 3D.

C071.name: AR Toolkit tracking library
C071.definition: This library provided real-time computer vision based tracking of a square marker.

C072.name: Mobile phone based AR application
C072.definition: This refers to the first demonstration of an augmented reality application utilizing a mobile phone.

C073.name: Commercial phase
C073.definition: This phase is characterized by AR experiences starting to become very popular, beginning with the launch of widely used consumer AR games.

C074.name: ARKit SDK
C074.definition: This is the SDK launched by Apple in 2017 for AR system development.

C075.name: ARCore
C075.definition: This is the SDK released by Google for Android OS or Android platforms.

C076.name: Commercial growth phase
C076.definition: This is the current phase where more applications and tools are expected to become available, with continuous improvements in hardware and algorithms.

C077.name: Issues and challenges
C077.definition: These are the problems and difficulties that exist within virtual and augmented reality systems.

C078.name: Synonyms
C078.definition: The terms augmented reality and mixed reality are used interchangeably and are considered synonyms.

C079.name: Virtual reality system
C079.definition: An artificial environment which is experienced through sensory stimuli provided by a computer, in which one's actions partially determine what happens in the environment.

C080.name: Objective of any VR system
C080.definition: To let the user experience an artificial environment through sensory stimuli provided by the computer.

C081.name: Technological issue
C081.definition: The challenge of how to generate suitable stimuli to experience the virtual or artificial environment.

C082.name: Psychological issue
C082.definition: The challenge of how the user perceives the generated stimuli, which relates to the role of the human factor and psychological characteristics.

C083.name: Immersion
C083.definition: Immersion is the objective degree to which a VR system and application projects stimuli onto the sensory receptors of users in a way that is extensive, matching, surrounding, vivid, interactive and plot informing.

C084.name: Extensive
C084.definition: Extensive refers to the range of sensory modalities that are presented to the user.

C085.name: Matching
C085.definition: Matching refers to the congruence between sensory modalities, such as appropriate visual presentation corresponding to head motion.

C086.name: Vivid
C086.definition: Vivid is the quality of energy stimulated within a particular modality, which relates to how much energy the computer is generating to stimulate that sensory organ.

C087.name: Interactivity
C087.definition: Interactivity refers to the capability of the user to make changes to the world, the response of virtual entities to user actions, and the user's ability to influence future events.

C088.name: Presence
C088.definition: Presence is a psychological state or subjective perception where the individual fails to accurately acknowledge the role of the technology in their current experience.

C089.name: Qualities
C089.definition: These qualities refer to the activation of one or more sensory organs in a suitable way.

C090.name: Psychological side
C090.definition: The psychological side is the domain of presence, relating to the user's subjective perception of the experience.

C091.name: Overall goal of any virtual reality system
C091.definition: The overall goal of any virtual reality system is to create a high degree of presence, making users feel they are in the virtual world and unable to distinguish it from the real world.

C092.name: Representational fidelity
C092.definition: It is the degree to which the VR experience conveys a place that is or could be on Earth.

C093.name: Combine real and virtual worlds
C093.definition: This requirement means that virtual content should be overlaid on the real world representation.

C094.name: Interactive in real time
C094.definition: This refers to supporting suitable forms of interaction so that the user can interact with the digital content overlaid on the real world representation.

C095.name: Pose
C095.definition: In this context, pose refers to two things: position and orientation.

C096.name: Registration phase
C096.definition: This phase determines the pose of a viewer with respect to the real world anchor.

C097.name: Tracking phase
C097.definition: This phase is necessary because the user is likely to move with an AR application, requiring continuous updates to the pose.

C098.name: Immersion
C098.definition: Immersion is tied to the technological aspect, the technological issues of VR.

C099.name: Cyber sickness
C099.definition: Cyber sickness is a concern that will be discussed in terms of its causes, measurement, and mitigation strategies.
